justifications.functional_suitability: All functional requirements are comprehensively supported: video consultations via Consultation Session Manager and WebRTC Media Broker, e-prescriptions via Prescription Orchestrator and FHIR & E-Prescription Integration Service, AI symptom checking via AI Symptom Checker Service, and granular consent management via Consent Manager Component.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Performance and scale are addressed with Mediasoup SFU, Redis caching in Fallback & Caching Engine, Regional Memorystore, asynchronous Cloud Pub/Sub messaging, and adaptive bitrate management to preserve bandwidth.
justifications.compatibility: FHIR Transformer explicitly implements US Core profiles and national EU standards (eHDSI/OpenNCP) to satisfy R-08. WebRTC Media Broker ensures standard protocol compliance (ICE/STUN/TURN, DTLS-SRTP) with external media infrastructure.
justifications.usability: Distinct client applications serve both user roles: Patient Portal App and Clinician Workspace App. Specialized UI components like AI Symptom Checker UI Module and E-Prescription & FHIR Viewer provide tailored workflows.
justifications.reliability: Low-bandwidth and rural degradation (<300 kbit/s) are handled via Degraded Mode Adaptor and Adaptive Bitrate Controller. Resilience is bolstered by Local State & Storage Manager offline caching and Pub/Sub Dead Letter Queue handlers.
justifications.security: Stringent residency (R-05) and regulatory needs are enforced by Data Residency Guard, Region-Aware State Sanitizer, OPA-based Consent Manager, mTLS & Security Terminator, regional CMEK encryption via GCP KMS, and WORM storage for immutable audits.
justifications.maintainability: Modular microservice architecture cleanly separates concerns between core telehealth, AI orchestration, regulatory consent, and prescription routing. Event Schema Registry and gRPC interfaces ensure low coupling and testability.
justifications.portability: The design directly maps to the target GCP environment across europe-west3 and us-central1 regions. Abstracted persistence interfaces (Storage Abstraction Layer) and containerized runtimes (Cloud Run, GKE) facilitate consistent multi-region execution.

PERF-01.justification: The architecture incorporates Mediasoup-based SFU routing, regional endpoint routing, and dedicated session management. Joining within 10 seconds is achievable, though SFU autoscaling and node allocation under sudden regional flu-season spikes depend heavily on underlying GKE and media broker elasticity.
sensitivity_points: SFU worker allocation and media port scaling during high concurrency
Signaling latency across API Gateway and room manager
tradeoffs: Selective Forwarding Unit resource usage versus peer-to-peer connection quality

PERF-02.justification: A load of 50,000 requests per hour (~14 requests/second) is low. The asynchronous FastAPI inference controller, Redis caching layer, and decoupled asynchronous Pub/Sub audit logging ensure p95 latency remains well below the 3-second threshold.
sensitivity_points: External AI inference provider latency and timeout thresholds
Redis cache hit rates for recurring symptom evaluation queries
tradeoffs: Immediate response latency versus depth of real-time external model inference

AVAIL-01.justification: The design explicitly includes client-side and server-side adaptive bitrate controllers alongside a degraded mode adaptor. Furthermore, the local state manager (IndexedDB/SQLite) preserves clinical notes offline during connection degradation below 300 kbit/s.
sensitivity_points: Accurate detection of bandwidth degradation threshold at 200 kbit/s
Client-side persistence sync consistency after connectivity restoration
tradeoffs: Degrading video stream quality to audio-only to preserve session continuity

AVAIL-02.justification: The system brief specifies only two cloud regions: europe-west3 and us-central1. While data residency prevents US data from being moved to the EU, there is no secondary US region defined to restore US services within 1 hour during a complete us-central1 outage.
sensitivity_points: Absence of multi-region deployment within the US territory
RTO compliance without violating cross-border data transfer constraints
tradeoffs: Strict regional residency prevents using EU infrastructure as a disaster recovery fallback

MOD-01.justification: Modifications are cleanly encapsulated within the dedicated FHIR & E-Prescription Integration Service. The FHIR Transformer and E-Prescription Router abstract country-specific standards (eHDSI/OpenNCP), leaving Core Telehealth and other upstream services untouched.
sensitivity_points: Completeness of abstraction in the internal canonical prescription data model
Country gateway connectivity protocols and authentication profiles
tradeoffs: Centralized integration service complexity versus per-country bespoke microservices

MOD-02.justification: The architecture satisfies EU MDR traceability: the Symptom Checker Gateway forwards model metadata, the Inference Controller tracks versions, and the Audit & Traceability Logger commits inputs, outputs, and model IDs immutably to WORM storage.
sensitivity_points: Strict coupling of model version identifiers with inference input payloads
Immutability guarantees of WORM storage buckets
tradeoffs: Comprehensive regulatory audit logging overhead versus raw inference throughput

SEC-01.justification: Cross-region access is intercepted by the Consent Enforcement Interceptor and evaluated by Open Policy Agent in the Consent Manager. Data Residency Guards and WORM audit logging ensure unauthorized requests are rejected and logged.
sensitivity_points: Policy evaluation latency and freshness in the Consent Manager
Immutability of cross-region access audit records
tradeoffs: Synchronous consent verification latency versus strict regulatory access enforcement

SEC-02.justification: Consent updates are received via the Consent API Handler and enforced across services via the OPA Consent Manager. Crypto-shredding sub-components and immutable audit logging enable verifiable and immediate cessation of research data sharing well within 24 hours.
sensitivity_points: Propagation delay of consent revocation across regional policy engines
Key revocation speed in crypto-shredding implementations
tradeoffs: Immediate crypto-shredding rendering data unrecoverable versus soft logical flags

elements: National E-Prescription Gateways & US Pharmacy Networks
